parts.text: Suggest what features your programmed revision exercises would include.

text: You want to devise a set of revision exercises for your psychology examination that can be done
on a computer. You decide that it will be based on what behaviourists call ‘programmed learning’.

parts.text: Suggest what you would do as a teacher to manage classroom behaviour effectively.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the psychology on which your suggestion in part (a) is based. 
Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: You are training to be a teacher. Some teachers you have observed keep discipline by correcting
a disruptive behaviour when it happens. You think that it would be much better to manage a
classroom effectively so problems are prevented from starting.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what is meant by an ‘objective measure of non-adherence to medical advice’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study of non-adherence to medical advice which used an objective measure.

Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about health and safety.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“It’s not my fault!” Evaluate what psychologists have learned about health and safety and
include a discussion of the issue of individual versus situational explanations.

Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would test the reliability and validity of any physiological recording device.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one study which has measured stress physiologically using a recording device.

text: Stress can be measured physiologically using recording devices and sample tests.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would test the long-term effectiveness of a snapshot study which attempts
to stop people from smoking.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one health promotion snapshot study. 
Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Some health promotion studies are snapshot because they take only a few hours to do. Often
such studies claim they are effective because when leaving the study people say they will change
their behaviour. But how does anyone know if they really will change their behaviour?

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘shopping mall atmospherics’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study which has investigated shopping mall atmospherics. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have learned about natural disaster and technological
catastrophe.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“If we can’t deceive people into thinking an experiment is a real emergency, what can we
do?” Evaluate what psychologists have learned about natural disaster and technological
catastrophe, including a discussion of the usefulness of simulations. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would conduct a study where the measure of pro-social behaviour is valid.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one study on the effects of crowding on pro-social behaviour.

text: Dukes and Jorgenson did a study on the effects of crowding on pro-social behaviour where people
helped by returning dirty dishes after a meal. However, returning dirty dishes may not be a valid
measure of pro-social behaviour.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would investigate car parking behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Using examples, describe psychological research on defending public territory. 
Psychology and Abnormality
Section A
Answer this question.

text: According to Ruback, drivers in the United States leave parking spaces more slowly when
someone is waiting to park their car in that space than when no-one is waiting. It is suggested that
this is because the driver leaving that space is defending the public territory they have occupied.

parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘cognitive-behaviour therapy’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe cognitive-behaviour therapy for obsessions and compulsions.

Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about abnormal affect.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“One day everything will be explained using biology.” Evaluate what psychologists have found
out about abnormal affect and include a discussion about biological explanations.

parts.text:

Psychology and Organisations
Section A
Answer this question.

text: A case study has the advantage of gathering lots of unique data about an individual, but has the
disadvantage that the data may not apply to other people.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘measuring job satisfaction’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one way in which job satisfaction has been measured.

Answer this question.

parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about organisational work conditions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
“It might be too bright in here for you, but it is fine for me.” Evaluate what psychologists have
learned about organisational work conditions and include a discussion about individual
differences.

parts.text:
Suggest how you would conduct an interview for a job that gave an equal opportunity to all
applicants.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the selection procedures on which your suggestion is based.

text: Equal opportunities: where there is no discrimination about age, race, sexual orientation or
disability.
